scope: Disposable single-host laboratory only; no production capacity admission
database_storage: disposable container writable layer; actual filesystem capacity/IO observations retained separately

concurrency_per_process.1: worker0 and worker1 run sequentially, one lane each

workload_mix: 1 event append plus one stream read of up to 16 events per sample
event_payload: seed73491, integer sample,128 ASCII x padding bytes
hot_stream_cardinality: same independent stream cardinality as uniform; one shared preinitialized admission-row counter/guard
arrival_model: closed-loop; one outstanding sample per lane, no external unbounded arrival queue
offered_rate: derived from measured completion time at predeclared concurrency; no fixed open-loop arrival-rate claim
failure_interval: separate declared connection-loss/restart test after each adapter sweep; resume and compare retained event/receipt/view state
acceptance: zero correctness violations and bounds breaches; report each unmeasured metric explicitly instead of approving capacity
comparison: identical hardware, source fixture, offered concurrency, data sizes and DB budget; adapter-internal baseline serialization versus candidate pool size is the measured implementation difference
supersedes_before_measurement: eventlog-comparative-lab-v3; previous v3b and intermediate receipts remain distinct pre-publication-fix evidence
transaction_observation: server pg_stat_statements or sampled pg_stat_activity; end-to-end append latency reported separately from guard lock/read time
warmup_interval: same live process/pool before the measured steady phase; excluded from worker steady throughput and latency histograms
compiler_policy: Both adapters use the identical compiler recorded before their builds in identity.json; each compiler change creates a distinct receipt.
candidate_publication_protocol: Owner shared writer / exclusive feed-and-rebuild transaction advisory gate with forced READ COMMITTED snapshots; original committed-XID predicate retained.
revision_reason: Corrected publication ordering protocol, complete source provenance, and current stable compiler; workloads, samples, resources and acceptance budgets unchanged.
